title: Three hundred pages of weather
summary_es: Dos críticos discuten, con mucha ironía y sin ponerse de acuerdo, sobre la novela de la que todo el mundo habla.
prediction_prompt: Two critics disagree about a much-praised novel. What kinds of things might they argue about?

segments.speaker: imogen
segments.text: So, the novel everyone has been told to adore. Dale, were you duly swept away?

segments.speaker: dale
segments.text: Swept, no. Mildly dampened, perhaps. It's three hundred pages of weather.

segments.speaker: imogen
segments.text: Oh, come on. The prose is extraordinary. That opening storm is a tour de force.

segments.speaker: dale
segments.text: It is. And then it rains again on page forty, and again on page ninety.

segments.speaker: dale
segments.text: At some point a metaphor stops being a metaphor and becomes a climate.

segments.speaker: imogen
segments.text: You're being glib. The weather is the grief. She can't say it, so the sky says it for her.

segments.speaker: dale
segments.text: I got that. I got it the first time.

segments.speaker: dale
segments.text: I didn't need it hammered home for an entire winter.

segments.speaker: imogen
segments.text: I'd call it patience rather than hammering. She trusts the reader to sit with discomfort.

segments.speaker: dale
segments.text: Does she? Or does she simply not know how to end a chapter?

segments.speaker: imogen
segments.text: That's unfair, and you know it. The ending of part two had me in pieces.

segments.speaker: dale
segments.text: The letter. Yes. I'll grant you the letter. It's the one moment she lets something actually happen.

segments.speaker: imogen
segments.text: Things happen throughout. They just happen quietly.

segments.speaker: dale
segments.text: Imogen, a man repairs a fence for eleven pages.

segments.speaker: imogen
segments.text: And by the end of those pages you know everything about his marriage. That's craft.

segments.speaker: dale
segments.text: It's craft, I don't dispute it. My worry is that craft is all it is.

segments.speaker: dale
segments.text: Every sentence has been polished until you can see the author's face in it.

segments.speaker: imogen
segments.text: Whereas you'd prefer something rough round the edges.

segments.speaker: dale
segments.text: I'd prefer something at stake. A book can be beautifully made and still feel airless.

segments.speaker: imogen
segments.text: Airless is harsh. Restrained, I'd say. And restraint is rather out of fashion.

segments.speaker: imogen
segments.text: Which may be your real objection.

segments.speaker: dale
segments.text: Possibly. I'll admit I'm allergic to novels that arrive already wearing their prizes.

segments.speaker: imogen
segments.text: Now we're getting somewhere. You resent the hype, not the book.

segments.speaker: dale
segments.text: A bit of both. If I'd found it in a second-hand shop, I might have loved it.

segments.speaker: imogen
segments.text: That says more about you than about her.

segments.speaker: dale
segments.text: It usually does. That's criticism for you.

segments.speaker: imogen
segments.text: So where does that leave our listeners?

segments.speaker: dale
segments.text: Read the first chapter in the shop. If the storm thrills you, buy it. You'll be happy for weeks.

segments.speaker: dale
segments.text: If you find yourself checking how many pages are left, put it back gently and walk away.

segments.speaker: imogen
segments.text: And I'd say: buy it, read it slowly, and don't let anyone tell you nothing happens.

segments.speaker: dale
segments.text: Least of all me.

segments.speaker: imogen
segments.text: Least of all you.

connected_speech.explanation_es: *were* se reduce a /wə/ y *swept away* se enlaza.

connected_speech.phrase: I got it the first time
connected_speech.explanation_es: En americano la *t* de *got it* suena casi como una «r» suave, y *first* pierde la *t* final.

connected_speech.phrase: I didn't need it hammered home
connected_speech.explanation_es: *didn't* pierde la *t* y *need it* se dice seguido.
*me in* se enlaza; el acento cae en *pieces*.
La *t* de *don't* desaparece y *dispute it* se une.

connected_speech.phrase: that craft is all it is
connected_speech.explanation_es: *all it is* se dice de un tirón; el último *is* lleva acento.
*I'd* = *I had*. Casi no se oye: lo delata *found*.

tasks.prompt: What do the two critics mainly disagree about?

options.text: Whether the novel's restraint is a strength or a weakness
Whether the author really deserved all her literary prizes or not
Whether the novel is too long

tasks.rationale_es: Para Imogen la contención es mérito; para Dale, falta de vida.

tasks.prompt: What is the tone of their exchange?

options.text: Bitter and personal
Sparring but good-humoured
Polite and noncommittal

tasks.rationale_es: Se pinchan sin parar, pero acaban riéndose de sí mismos.

tasks.prompt: What does Dale mean by "three hundred pages of weather"?

options.text: The book contains accurate meteorology
A single image is used to excess
The plot takes place outdoors in winter

tasks.rationale_es: La metáfora del tiempo se repite tanto que deja de serlo.

tasks.prompt: According to Imogen, what does the weather stand for?

options.text: The narrator's unspoken sorrow
The slow passing of time in the countryside
The husband's anger

tasks.rationale_es: Lo que la narradora no puede decir lo dice el cielo.

tasks.prompt: "I didn't need it hammered home" means Dale felt the point was…

options.text: too subtle to notice
made too insistently
factually wrong

tasks.rationale_es: *Hammer home* = remachar. Lo entendió a la primera.

tasks.prompt: Dale thinks the letter scene is the weakest part of the book.
tasks.rationale_es: Al contrario: es lo único que le concede a Imogen.

tasks.prompt: Why does Imogen say the fence scene reveals the man's marriage?

options.text: To show that the plot is confusing
To prove the book is really about farming life
To argue that quiet scenes carry meaning

tasks.rationale_es: Defiende que en esas páginas «en las que no pasa nada» se cuenta mucho.

tasks.prompt: What is Dale's deeper worry about the novel?

options.text: It is skilful but lacks urgency
It is badly written from start to finish
It is too emotional

tasks.rationale_es: Reconoce el oficio; teme que no haya nada más.

tasks.prompt: A novel that "arrives already wearing its prizes" is one that…

options.text: is sold with a free gift
has been heavily praised before you read it
was written only in order to win major awards

tasks.rationale_es: Llega ya consagrada, y eso le predispone en contra.

tasks.prompt: Imogen suggests Dale's objection is partly to the publicity rather than to the book.
tasks.rationale_es: *You resent the hype, not the book*.

tasks.prompt: What does Dale concede with "It usually does. That's criticism for you"?

options.text: That reviews reveal the reviewer's own tastes
That he has not actually finished reading the book yet
That Imogen is the better critic

tasks.rationale_es: Admite que una crítica habla tanto del crítico como de la obra.

tasks.prompt: What does Dale advise listeners to do?

options.text: Wait for the paperback
Avoid the book entirely and read something else
Sample the opening before deciding

tasks.rationale_es: Leer el primer capítulo en la librería y decidir.

tasks.prompt: By the end, the two critics reach complete agreement.
tasks.rationale_es: Cada uno mantiene su consejo; solo coinciden en reírse de Dale.
